findings.finding: Nike's FY27 guide assumed incremental tariffs of 10% through July then 15% thereafter, but when Section 122 expired on 2026-07-24 it was replaced by a Section 301 tariff of 10% or 12.5% depending on the country (Vietnam at 12.5%), so the rate on goods landing from August is 2.5-5 points below plan, a gross-margin tailwind that can only show up in the Q2/H2 margin guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY26 (2026-06-30): fell ~8% after hours on the cautious Q1 outlook and closed +4.9% once the call pulled gross-margin expansion forward to Q1 (sweep row, CNBC); margin-timing has been the line that reversed the last reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Piper Sandler cut its Q1 gross margin by 40bp on 2026-09-28 and UBS/Piper sit 12% below Street on Q2, i.e. the visible sell-side revisions run the other way; if the lower actual rate were in numbers, Q2 margin estimates would have moved up after July, not down. Nike's own assumption of 15% (transcript p.12) is the stale input. Caveat carried in the size: the rate is litigated (25 states sued at the CIT) and flows through inventory with a lag, so Q1 itself barely sees it.
findings.independence: Nike's 15% assumption is from the company transcript https://s1.q4cdn.com/806093406/files/doc_financials/2026/q4/NIKE-Inc-Q4FY26-OFFICIAL-Transcript_-FINAL.pdf ; the actual 10%/12.5% Vietnam tier is corroborated by https://tradewithviet.com/blog/vietnam-us-tariff-2026/ . Macro-to-company transmission, not confirmed by Nike: a proxy.

findings.finding: Nike's largest North American wholesale partners reported sell-through weakness over the June-August window after Nike last spoke: JD Sports North America like-for-like -6.8% in the 13 weeks to 1 August with Nike over 40% of JD's sales and a profit-guide cut, and Foot Locker comps -3.6% at Dick's, blamed on legacy and retro footwear and an increasingly promotional market; BofA's downgrade cites the gap between Nike's NA wholesale growth and sell-through, which points at a softer Q2/H2 sell-in guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 (2026-03-31) beat and fell -15.5% close-to-close on a weak Q4 guide; Q2 FY26 (2025-12-18) fell -10.5% — the guide is what this name trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: Dick's fell ~30% on 2026-08-25 and the read-across to Nike ran on the wire (Yahoo, MediaPost), BofA and Baird downgraded on it, and NKE is -6% over 20 days at a 13-year low. What remains unpriced is the size of the sell-in cut Nike announces; Nike itself said in June it is tightening buys and reducing sell-in, so part of this lands inside its own guide, which is why the size is small.
findings.independence: JD Sports Q2 trading/guidance cut https://www.abcmoney.co.uk/2026/09/jd-sports-cuts-profit-guidance-as-north-america-sales-slide (2026-08-20, different company); BofA downgrade https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9099067/bank-of-america-downgrades-nike-nke-amid-prolonged-turnaround-cuts-price-target-to-30 (2026-09-26). Counterweight netted into the size: Dick's management said Nike running (Nike Mind) and Solo fleece were working 'extremely well'.

findings.finding: China retail kept falling through the quarter: Pou Sheng (Yue Yuen's China retail arm, a Nike and Adidas reseller) posted August revenue -9% y/y and Topsports' March-May sales fell by a low-teens percentage, while Nike's own termination of online authorisations for thousands of China resellers from 2027-01-01 adds a headwind to the H2 China guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 FY26 (2025-12-18) fell -10.5% with China cited as the drag; Q4 FY26 China -17% did not stop a +4.9% close.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: Nike guided China 'in line with recent performance' (Q4 -17%) and consensus already has Greater China around -12.6%; the online-reseller cut was public on 2026-07-22 (Topsports -30% that day). Pou Sheng -9% includes a growing Adidas, so Nike's share is likely worse, but the incremental surprise is small and sits inside the guide.
findings.independence: Topsports/Nike online cut https://finance.sina.com.cn/stock/s/2026-07-22/doc-iniisttv1904310.shtml (2026-07-22); Piper Sandler note citing Pou Sheng declines in July and August https://investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/piper-sandler-cuts-nike-stock-price-target-on-worsening-trends-93CH-4920635 (2026-09-28) — it reads the same Pou Sheng series, so not independent of the source.

findings.finding: Street Q2 EPS of $0.53 already sits on the ceiling of Nike's own 'flattish earnings ex-tariff-recovery' framework for Q4 FY26-Q2 FY27 (prior-year $0.14 + $0.49 + $0.53 = $1.16; Q4 FY26 ex-benefit delivered $0.20, so Q1+Q2 needs ~$0.96 against consensus $0.44 + $0.53 = $0.97), while Nike pre-flagged a multipoint sequential revenue deceleration into Q2 and UBS expects an implied Q2 of $0.31-0.43.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26: beat, guide below Street, -15.5%; Q4 FY26: guide composition shifted (revenue lower, margin earlier), AH -8% then +4.9% close.
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic says the Street is exactly at the company's framework, so a reiteration is neutral and any shortfall is a cut; bears (UBS, Piper -12% on Q2) are on record, so a cut to ~$0.45 is partly expected, which is why the size is small. If fully priced, consensus Q2 would already sit below $0.53 rather than at it.
findings.independence: Prior-year EPS from Nike's Q2 FY26 and Q4 FY25 releases https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320187/000032018725000138/q2fy26exhibit991er.htm and https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320187/000032018725000034/q4fy25exhibit991er.htm ; Q1 FY26 $0.49 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/320187/000032018725000091/q1fy26exhibit991er.htm . Shares the sell-side read with the Piper note in finding 3 only for the Q2-below-Street view. The lower tariff rate (finding 1) is the offset and is filed separately with the opposite sign; they are not contradictory — revenue/demand versus cost rate.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 FY26 (2026-06-30): a de-rated name with a cautious guide reversed from -8% after hours to +4.9%; Q1 FY26 (2025-09-30) +6.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, so its weight is small: if the market were positioned for a relief rally the 25-delta skew would not still pay for downside (+2.03) and the stock would not be 1.5% off its 52w low. Days to cover under 3 limits the squeeze mechanism.
